findings.evidence: object FORM changed while arrangement held: rectangular fringed rug -> round braided rug; tall dark bookshelf with vertical spines -> low bookcase with front-facing picture books; straight plank walls -> curved barrel walls
findings.specified: cottage_night names 'a woven rug' and 'a low bookshelf' but describes neither's shape or construction. The prompt's FIXED LAYOUT block pins POSITIONS only.

findings.evidence: legible lettering on the book covers
findings.specified: the frame prompt ends with the literal instruction 'No text or lettering.' and the video constraint clause forbids text as well. Both were ignored.

diagnosis.correction: An earlier verdict said the bed was repositioned and the room 'rebuilt'. That was wrong. Checking the output against the prompt's FIXED LAYOUT line: window LEFT, bookshelf FAR LEFT, bed RIGHT, chair beside the bed, rug centre floor — every position was obeyed.
diagnosis.what_actually_failed: Prose pinned every object's POSITION and none of their FORM. The layout instruction worked. There is no sentence in the bible describing what the rug or the bookshelf LOOK like, so the model chose, and chose differently from s01.
diagnosis.why_here_first: s04 is the first shot needing to show more of the world than its reference contained. s03 is a CLOSE on a sleeping bear; the rug and bookshelf are simply not in it, so there were no pixels to copy and only prose to go on.
diagnosis.structural_gap: Characters have pixel authority (portraits, injected every frame). Locations have only prose. Text controls arrangement well and appearance not at all — which is exactly the gap a location plate closes.
diagnosis.not_a_general_defect: WIDE->CLOSE held perfectly at s01->s02. Narrowing needs no invention. Widening is the unsupported direction.
diagnosis.text_violation_is_separate: 'No text or lettering' was in the prompt verbatim and was ignored. That is a provider compliance failure, not a missing-reference failure, and a location plate will not fix it.
